label: Revision-authored AQA-style practice question (original, not an AQA question)

question.context: Revision-authored AQA-style practice. Lakeside Components has reliable business customers owing £120,000, payable in 70 days. It needs cash soon to buy materials; its invoices are genuine and collectable.
question.stem: Which is the most accurate assessment of using debt factoring in this situation?

options.label: A
options.text: Factoring could release cash tied up in receivables earlier, usually in return for fees and possible customer-relationship considerations.

options.label: B
options.text: Factoring guarantees the company an extra £120,000 of sales revenue and profit immediately.

options.label: C
options.text: Factoring converts the business into a publicly listed company, raising equity capital.

options.label: D
options.text: Factoring is always cheaper than using retained profit and carries no disadvantages.

option_rationale: A is correct because a factor may provide cash against invoices before their normal due date, but fees and customer interaction should be considered.
B is incorrect because earlier receipt of existing debt does not create new sales revenue or necessarily increase accounting profit.
C is incorrect because debt factoring is not an issue of ordinary shares.
D is incorrect because factoring can be costly and is not universally superior to internal funding.
mark_scheme.model_answer: A. Factoring can accelerate cash receipts against receivables, at a cost; compare fees, customer relationships and suitability with alternative short-term finance.
